## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`--json` consumes a following flag as its destination, so the default JSON destination fails whenever `--json` precedes `--junit`; this must be fixed before merge because it breaks the combination the pull request describes.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `--json` option to `parse_args` that takes an explicit path or falls back to `results.json`, and adds `write_reports`, which writes each report to its parsed destination. It also adds `tests/test_cli.py` covering the JSON default, an explicit JSON path, and the required `--junit` path.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Keep the JSON default when the next argument is a flag — `--json --junit out.xml` stores `--junit` as the JSON destination, then raises `unknown option: out.xml`. `--json --junit` returns `{"json": "--junit"}`, so `write_reports` writes a file named `--junit`. Line 15 checks only that a next argument exists, unlike the `--junit` check at line 7. — Users who put `--json` before another flag get a rejected command line or a report written to a file named after the flag. — Fix: Apply the `startswith("--")` check from `app/cli.py:7` to the conditions at lines 15 and 18, and extend `test_json_default_and_explicit_path` with a `--json` followed by `--junit` case.
